function.mechanism: Chelates polyvalent metal ions (e.g., iron and copper), reducing metal-catalyzed oxidation and preserving color/flavor/texture.

adi.basis: Current ADI as EDTA in EFSA 2018 opinion context; equivalent to 2.5 mg/kg bw/day as calcium disodium EDTA.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA reported no scientific justification to increase the current ADI; re-evaluation call workflow indicates assessment completion targeted by end of 2026.

adi.basis: JECFA ADI expressed as 0-2.5 mg/kg bw/day for calcium disodium EDTA.

concerns.summary: Legacy toxicology reports renal injury mainly under high parenteral exposure conditions, supporting conservative oral ADI management.
Chelation may alter essential mineral handling at high exposures; infant/high-intake scenarios were highlighted in EFSA ferric sodium EDTA exposure context.

no_concern_confirmed: Low oral absorption with predominantly fecal excretion in older ADME data.
FDA permits use with explicit category limits in 21 CFR 172.120.
JECFA and EFSA maintain numeric ADIs rather than withdrawing authorization.

populations: High-intake infants (scenario in EFSA ferric sodium EDTA assessment context)
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA indicated potential high-intake exceedance in infant scenario modeling; a 2026 beverage survey found higher relative exposure in children, though overall HI remained below 1 in that dataset.

risk_assessment.rationale: E385 remains approved with ADI-based controls, but available evidence supports non-trivial caveats for high-intake groups (especially infants/children) and high-dose toxicity context.
key_factors: ADI maintained by EFSA/JECFA rather than ADI-not-specified
FDA authorization is conditional with explicit ppm limits
No IARC carcinogenic group assignment identified
